issue_context.title: Terminal key bindings do not work as expected
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it

The integrated terminal in Zed seems to rewrite the custom key bindings I have in my zsh config:
```zsh
bindkey "^[[1;5C" forward-word
bindkey "^[[1;5D" backward-word
bindkey '^H' backward-kill-word
```

### Environment

Zed: v0.139.0 (Zed Nightly 94c3101fb0ecbaf5f322dd7b94c239f8a66a5a5f)
OS: Linux 1.0.0
Memory: 30.5 GiB
Architecture: x86_64

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature

Konsole:

[Screencast_20240601_113614.webm](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/assets/71973804/77857d37-4719-406b-b4bf-6c8bba366bfa)

Zed:

[Screencast_20240601_113739.webm](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/assets/71973804/94ab7bbb-8242-4971-8c69-d038248ff8fc)


### If applicable, attach your `~/Library/Logs/Zed/Zed.log` file to this issue.

_No response_

review_comments: I used the Control-H key here since that's what Konsole and Gnome Terminal send when doing Ctrl+Backspace. VSCode sends `\x1b\x7f` like when doing Alt+Backspace.
I think I'd prefer if we didn't make this change, everything else being equal. Could it be Linux-only?

This seems to be the expected behaviour: https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/issues/7100#issuecomment-1645035896
Asides, if the keymap overwrites the keybinding (like in macOS, where I did not change it) it takes precedence over the code here.
Oh excellent. We should stick to alacritty then. Thanks for clarifying :)
